messages.subject: PK modeling using random effects
parts:
Hi,

Inspired by the post of random intercepts and slopes I have rewritten the model to utilize the code in

https://00335207212371662729.googlegroups.com/attach/e3d980b13d0bbd04/vasishth2.stan?part=2&view=1&vt=ANaJVrEXlW3LhFzaeRT5gwRyx39I9sAUpxQIbtlbtte9lY1ByVmLhoqIL4J7qkhSaNfLLK4TtQ9Yj1EX8uC2nyXKgRA7iehnxWEo4h1Ma-KcqBj5SDsAWLE

but with limited success.  I have 17 subjects and each subject has five parameters.  The sampling statement is
    for (i in 1 : NP) {                            // loop for subj random effects
            u [i] ~ multi_normal_cholesky (mu_prior, DL);
    }
where NP=17 - the number of subjects.  Each subject is described by NPAR=5 parameters. By changing the declaration of random effect u from
    vector [NPAR] u [NP]; // subj random effects
to
    vector [NP] u [NPAR]; // subj random effects
I was able to transition from error message
Error : INDEX OPERATOR [] OUT OF BOUNDS; index=6; lower bound=1; upper bound=5; index position=2; u
to
Error in function stan::prob::multi_normal_cholesky_log(x): Size of random variableSize of random variable (17) and size of location parameter (5) must match in sizeRejecting proposed initial value with zero density.
Initialization failed after 100 attempts.  Try specifying initial values, reducing ranges of constrained values, or reparameterizing the model.
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

It seems I messed up somewhere on declaration/assignment level since my random variable is of size 17 or number of subjects and the size of location parameter is 5 or number of parameters which describe a subject.  I am completely lost - any help is appreciated.  The stan code is attached.

Linas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] PK modeling using random effects
parts: vector [NPAR] mu_prior; //vector of zeros passed in from R

u[i] : vector[NP]

mu_prior: vector[NPAR]

DL : matrix[NPAR,NPAR]

So it looks like u has the definitions reversed. It should probably be:

vector[NPAR] u[NP];

The declaration for the vector part of this always stays together,
and the array indices are used first.

- Bob
